title: Pyrazinamide
dek: A nicotinamide analogue prodrug, PncA-activated, pH-dependent, sterilizing in acidic necrotic lesions. Whole-gene pncA, fussy MGIT, intrinsic R in M. bovis.
story: Pyrazinamide shortens DS-TB from 9–18 months toward 6 by hitting bacilli in acidic, inflammatory, necrotic niches where INH looks ordinary. PncA makes pyrazinoic acid; activity collapses as pH rises toward 7. That is why broth DST is a pH protocol and why caseum is the pharmacological home.

WHO intensive-phase dose ~25 mg/kg (child bands higher). Hepatotoxicity overlaps INH/RIF. Hyperuricemia and arthralgia are the other host notes (POA interferes with urate). Pregnancy: WHO keeps PZA; some older CDC overlays did not.
No RRDR. Sequence pncA. M. bovis/BCG intrinsic-R. See tb-pnca.
deepTitle: Sterilizing does not mean always necessary
deep: Continuation-phase DS-TB drops Z. HPMZ keeps Z only 2 months. Some 9-month DR recipes keep Z throughout if pncA is clean.
TBM: PZA is a CSF-friendly sterilizing companion — keep it unless the allele forbids.
panD/clpC1 are uncommon extras. Do not lead with them.

visual.caption: Schematic PZA activity versus pH. The clinical lesion sits left (acid); poorly acidified MGIT sits right (false S or chaos). PncA is assumed intact on this curve.

example.title: ALT 4× ULN on week 3 of HRZE
example.setup: Hepatitis, no alcohol, no viral hepatitis. Which first-line to blame first is a clinical art; PZA is a frequent culprit.

steps.title: Stop the likely hepatotoxins (INH/PZA/RIF) per NTP hepatitis SOP
steps.body: Do not keep PZA as a mascot while ALT climbs.

steps.title: Re-challenge in a planned order
steps.body: RIF is the sterilizing drug you most want back. PZA is the one many SOPs reintroduce last or not at all if severe.

steps.title: If PZA is retired, extend or rebuild
steps.body: Losing Z can mean a longer DS regimen. That is allowed. Silent 4-month HPMZ without Z is not.

example.takeaway: PZA buys shorter therapy in acid lesions and spends liver.
